rationale: Contract-stability/sequencing lens on 6f75235b. CORE ANSWER FIRST: I examined every tail-level assertion in agreement_table_test.go against bead 5's contracted changes (the indeterminate form in emitInstruct, spec-create's spec-mode tail, complete's NextMode agreement + ModePlan reword) and found NO assertion that pins a pre-bead-5 tail bead 5 must break. The suite asserts the phase-level template-selection inputs (ResolveContextFromDirWithCache -> instruct.BuildContextWithCache -> instruct.Render), never emitInstruct's cmd-layer fallback; every row wires HEALTHY bd seams, so bead 5's indeterminate trigger (context error or empty phase) can never apply to any fixture. Row-by-row stability: (1) spec-create wires bd-success-empty (not bd-failure), pinning the contracted ADR-0023 OQ-2 WorktreeSpec no-epic arm — stable even if bead 5 de-swallows derive.go's bd-failure fallbacks (the recorded bead-3 R3 carry-forward), because the fixture never drives the error arm; (2) the terminal row asserts success-discovery idle over bareGitRoot (a real repo with zero drafts and zero open epics) — deliberately robust both to a de-swallowed error propagation and to bead 5 making the WorktreeMain path draft-aware, and idle-on-successful-zero-discovery is exactly the arm bead 5 keeps (indeterminate replaces only the error/empty cases); (3) the four complete rows assert derivation/state-show/tail-input surfaces, never FormatResult text, and the guide quotes no command-output examples — so bead 5's ModePlan reword has the two complete->plan rows as its stable wording target, which is the CORRECT dependency direction (bead 4 supplies the rows the reworded message must fit, per R2.3/round-4 G1.3). Guide-vs-delivered-semantics sweep (beads 2/3): plan-approve writes plan under the lock with a backward-refuse no-op (plan.go:514-518) — matches row 3; advancePhaseOnClaim is lock-guarded, fresh-Cache re-deriving, writes implement only while derived==implement (next.go:561-580) — matches the forward-by-evidence bullet including the disclosed review->implement case; LegacyPhaseSignature's positive all-open check (semantics_v2.go:80-95) makes the blocked-child marker-absent epic non-legacy (no self-heal) — matches legacy shape 1's mechanism; step 4b preserves a present-but-invalid stored phase via IsBackwardMove's unknown->true conservatism (order.go:39-46) — matches legacy shape 2; SanctionedDerivedSync is release.go's one caller, in-lock, error-propagating — matches the release rows. The two run.go standalone-instruct windows (main-with-draft->idle; bd-failure->handleNoState idle) remain bead-5 carry-forwards and nothing in the guide contradicts their recorded status. TWO defects require changes, both cheap: (A) the guide's legacy-shapes bullet 1 misattributes the --force-backward recovery to 'the backward warning's named recovery' — the delivered backward-disagreement warning deliberately ends with the INSPECTION action `recovery: bd show <epic-id>` (derive.go:214-217, the AC-5(iv) design: the warning must NEVER name the backward write); --force-backward is named by repair phase's unforced refusal (repair.go:321) and release's sync-failure text (release.go:183). In a spec whose subject is exact message honesty, the bead's primary doc deliverable inverting a spec-pinned message property is a real error, one sentence to fix. (B) the commit trailer's 'no third-surface assertion was deferred to bead 5' is true at the assertion level but undisclosed at the verb-surface level for row 1: the fixture asserts the WorktreeSpec proxy path, while the spec-create verb's REAL tail (spec.go:78 emitInstruct -> cwd-based ResolveContext -> the WorktreeMain branch, which at this HEAD is NOT draft-aware, derive.go:626-634) still renders idle.md from the main checkout until bead 5 lands AC-3 (plan step 2) — the exact window the impl prompt's contingency ('record the third in Deviations naming bead 5, rather than papering over it') existed for. Not a sequencing defect (no fixture pins the broken path; bead 5 breaks nothing), but the disclosure is owed. Suite verified green at 6f75235b; worktree left byte-identical.

The backward-disagreement warning's own recovery line is the inspection action `bd show <epic-id>` (derive.go:214-217; AC-5(iv): the warning never names the backward write). The forced exit `mindspec repair phase <spec-id> --force-backward "<reason>"` is named by repair phase's unforced-refusal output (cmd/mindspec/repair.go:321) and by release's sync-failure text — reword the sentence to name that chain (warning -> inspect -> repair refusal -> --force-backward) instead of attributing --force-backward to the warning.

Nothing pins the broken path and bead 5 breaks no fixture — sequencing is sound — but the impl prompt's explicit Deviations-naming-bead-5 contingency was the honest route for this residue, and the trailer instead claims full coverage via template existence. One disclosure sentence resolves it.
